_about: Hand-maintained homework for one game. Keys: event (overrides: venue, kickoff_text, kickoff_iso, tv, sub_title, kicker, deadline_text), consensus (a sportsbook line to compare with), research (the Homework section). Delete the file and the card still renders from Kalshi alone.

event.venue: Pat Dye Field at Jordan-Hare Stadium, Auburn, AL
event.sub_title: College · Week 3 · SEC opener for both · Florida at Auburn

consensus.label: Sportsbook consensus
consensus.total_note: The board is split a full point: 53.5 at bet365, DraftKings and FanDuel; 53 at Fanatics; 52.5 at BetMGM, Caesars, Hard Rock and Rivers. Kalshi's contract is the 52.5, the low end of the market.

opener.spread: VSiN and TheSpread both say it opened Florida −2.5 and has not moved; VegasInsider says it opened PICK'EM. These are incompatible and the difference matters — see the conflict note.
opener.total: 52.5 per VSiN, 53 per TheSpread, 53.5 per VegasInsider
opener.moneyline: Florida −130 consensus; Hard Rock shortest at −135, Caesars longest at −120

injuries.source: SEC availability reports, Florida Sep 16 (updated Sep 17) and Auburn Sep 17 2026
injuries.FLA: QUESTIONABLE: WR Eric Singleton Jr. (ankle), DE Emmanuel Oyebadejo (lower body). PROBABLE: K Patrick Durkin. No quarterback on the report — Aaron Philo is healthy
injuries.AUB: OUT: OL Tai Buster. QUESTIONABLE: TE Hunter Herring, EDGE Joe Phillips. Not listed and expected to play: EDGE Da'Shawn Womack and EDGE Chris Murray, both of whom missed Week 2. No quarterback on the report — Byrum Brown is healthy

line.text: Florida −2.5 is the number at six of eight books, with BetMGM and Fanatics at −2 and Hard Rock hanging an odd −0.5 while simultaneously posting the shortest Florida moneyline on the board, which makes that row internally inconsistent and probably stale. The total has drifted DOWN at half the market, from 53.5 to 52.5 at BetMGM, Caesars, Hard Rock and Rivers. Nobody has taken the spread through 3.
line.kalshi: Kalshi asks 56¢ for Florida, which normalizes to 55.4% — at or above the top of the devigged sportsbook range of 52.8%–55.3%. Kalshi is the most Florida-heavy price available anywhere. Auburn at 45¢ normalizes to 44.6%, below every book's fair number and below all three neutral models.
line.src: VegasInsider Sep 19; FanDuel Research Sep 19; TheSpread Sep 19

splits.text: Spread tickets: 70% on Florida. The line has not moved. That is the classic shape of recreational money on the favourite being absorbed rather than chased.

TheSpread's own read: with 70% of tickets on Florida and a static number, 'the money behind the remaining 30 percent is heavier per ticket.' On the total, money shifted to the Over without moving the number off 53.
VSiN flagged expected Auburn buyback later in the week as likely to be 'quite sharp in nature', and asked which book would be first to −3 — nobody was.

line.conflict: No money or handle percentage exists for this game anywhere. SportsBettingDime states plainly it has no splits for it, Action Network returned stale 2024 data, Covers' consensus URL 404s. So 'sharp money on Auburn' is an inference from ticket-versus-line behaviour, not a measured split, and it should be read that way. The opener is also genuinely disputed: if VegasInsider is right that it opened pick'em, Florida has been bet up 2.5 points; if VSiN and TheSpread are right that it opened −2.5, then a 70% Florida ticket split has failed to move the number at all — which is a much stronger Auburn signal.

week1.head: Florida 2-0: beat Florida Atlantic 66-21 (Sep 5), beat Campbell 52-3 (Sep 12)
week1.text: The scorelines are enormous and the opposition was worthless. Florida is second in the FBS at 4.42 points per drive with a +3 turnover margin. Aaron Philo is 32 of 42 for 517 yards, five touchdowns and one pick at 12.3 yards an attempt, and Jadan Baugh leads the SEC in rushing with 296 yards on 28 carries. The context that matters: this is Jon Sumrall's first season after a near-total staff overhaul, Philo is in his tenth career game with 278 career snaps, and Saturday is HIS FIRST CAREER ROAD START. Florida went 0-6 outside The Swamp in 2025 and has not won at Auburn in 27 years. The defensive line has four sacks and is giving up 91 rushing yards a game.
week1.src: Florida Gators official Sep 17; Gainesville Sun Sep 18 2026

week1.head: Auburn 2-0: beat Baylor 17-16 in Atlanta (Sep 5), beat Southern Miss 43-8 (Sep 12)
week1.text: Auburn's résumé is the mirror image — it has already survived a real opponent by a point while Florida was beating up cupcakes. Alex Golesh is making his SEC coaching debut, but he brought Byrum Brown with him from South Florida: fifth college season, 35 career starts, roughly 2,450 career snaps against Philo's 278 — and Brown has already beaten Florida once, with USF. D.J. Durkin's defence has been retained and has allowed 20.3 points a game over three seasons, ninth nationally. Three Auburn backs rushed for 80-plus against Southern Miss for the first time since 2019. The weakness is the offensive line: eight penalties in two games and five sacks allowed to Baylor, and starter Tai Buster is out.
week1.src: Auburn Tigers official Sep 16; Montgomery Advertiser Sep 18 2026

injuries.as_of: Wednesday's SEC availability reports, Florida released Sep 16 8:32 PM ET and updated Sep 17, Auburn reported Sep 17. No Friday or gameday final report was found for either team, so Eric Singleton Jr. remains an unresolved game-time decision.
injuries.src: The Independent Florida Alligator Sep 16; SI / Auburn Daily Sep 17 2026
FLA: HEALTHY, starting. Not on the report. First career road start
QUESTIONABLE — out of the walking boot Monday, game-time decision. The single live injury variable in this game
AUB: HEALTHY, starting. Not on the report. 35 career starts
RETURNING — missed Week 2, not on the mandatory report
RETURNING — missed Week 2, not on the mandatory report
OUT — starting lineman, on a line that has already allowed five sacks in a game
injuries.read: Both starting quarterbacks are clean, so this is not a quarterback-availability game. The two items that matter point in the same direction: Florida's best perimeter weapon is a coin flip to play, and Auburn gets BOTH starting edge rushers back to attack a first-year starter making his first road start in a sold-out Jordan-Hare. Against that, Auburn loses a starting offensive lineman from a unit that is already its weak point.

weather.text: Hot, still, and with a real thunderstorm risk in the kickoff window. The NWS point forecast issued 9:01 AM CDT this morning has a high of 94°F, mostly sunny, wind calm becoming northeast around 5 mph, and a 40% chance of showers and thunderstorms mainly after 3 PM, continuing into the evening before 10 PM. For a 6:05 PM CT kick that means upper-80s at kickoff cooling through the game, effectively NO WIND, and a lightning-delay tail risk rather than a base case. Earlier and secondhand forecasts ran hotter on precipitation — 60% via Hail Florida Hail, 50% at 5 PM CT via Auburn Wire — but the gameday-morning issue is the one to trust. Wind is a non-factor in every source.
weather.src: NWS Birmingham point forecast for Auburn, issued 9:01 AM CDT Sep 19 2026

venue.text: Auburn expects its 24th consecutive sellout at Jordan-Hare. Auburn leads the series at home 26-8-1 and has won the last three home meetings and four of the last six overall; the last meeting was 2019, a 24-13 Florida win in Gainesville. Florida has not won at Auburn in 27 years. Worth flagging: the two athletics departments publish contradictory all-time series records — Auburn's site says Auburn leads 43-39-2, Florida's site says Florida leads 43-39-2, same numbers, opposite claimant.
venue.src: Auburn Tigers official Sep 16; Florida Gators official Sep 17 2026

voices.take: SP+ is the big Florida outlier at 63% and a projected 26-21, but it is dated Sep 14 and is rating Florida off two blowouts of FAU and Campbell. ESPN's FPI has it 50.4% Florida; ESPN's Matchup Predictor has Auburn 50.2%; numberFire has Florida 50.5%. So three independent neutral models call this a coin flip while the market says 53.5% Florida and Kalshi says 55.4%. SportsLine's 10,000 simulations project 58 combined points and take the Over 53.5 in 55% of runs, but its side pick is paywalled.

voices.who: Media picks look 8-3 Florida, but strip the homers and it is 4-3
voices.take: Four of the eight Florida picks are the Gators Wire panel, a Florida-affiliated outlet. The remaining split is Brockway (Gainesville Sun), Fiutak, TheRX and 1230 The Gambler for Florida; Adam Cole (Montgomery Advertiser, Auburn 34-28), Covers and SI Betting for Auburn. Notably the two most explicitly betting-focused outlets, Covers and SI Betting, are BOTH on Auburn +2.5.

voices.who: Covers' case for Auburn and the Under
voices.take: Florida's two wins came against inferior non-conference opponents while Auburn has already faced Baylor; both teams have offensive line depth problems. Covers takes Auburn +2.5, Under 53.5, and a Florida team total Under 27.5, citing Auburn hitting the Under in six of its last seven home games.

The Auburn Plainsman's writers' roundtable returned 403 and On3's Florida piece is paywalled. tracks.intro: Two of Ahmed's rows are picked by Claude, each by a fixed method, and placed through the same form as everyone else. Neither is the System: the System needs a live Pinnacle line and sits out until the collector runs.

research.method: Bet whatever most people think will win — sportsbook ticket counts, prediction-market crowds, expert panels, Reddit and X — at the best Kalshi price for that side.
research.verdict: The crowd is on Florida and it is not close: 70% of spread tickets, a favourite at every book, and the headline model. This track buys that at 56¢ knowing full well it is the richest Florida price available — which is precisely why the statistics track took the other side of the same game.

evidence.text: 70% of spread tickets are on Florida.
Named media picks run 8-3 Florida, including a 4-0 sweep by the Gators Wire panel, plus Brockway, Fiutak, TheRX and 1230 The Gambler.
evidence.src: Gators Wire / USA Today panel, Sep 16 2026

evidence.text: SP+ — the model most people quote — has Florida at 63% and a projected margin of 5.3, and ranks Florida 13th overall with the 10th-best defence.
Florida is favoured at every book on the board, −120 to −135, and has scored 66 and 52 while ranking second in the FBS in points per drive with the SEC's leading rusher.
Stake: 2,400 contracts at 56¢ = $1,344, fee $41.40, $1,385.40 tied up. Break-even 57.73¢.

statistics.method: Estimate each outcome's probability from models and the sharpest sportsbook prices, subtract Kalshi's ask and fee, and bet the line with the best expected profit — if there is one.
statistics.verdict: The only bet on the whole six-game board that clears the fee. Three neutral models call this a coin flip while Kalshi prices Auburn at 44.6% — below every model AND below the better sportsbook numbers. That is roughly a 3-4¢ gap against a 1.74¢ fee, so about +1.5 to +2.2¢ a contract. Thin, and said plainly: this is the least-wrong bet on the board, not a strong one. It rests on discounting SP+, which is the one model that loudly disagrees.

evidence.text: The three neutral models: ESPN Matchup Predictor has Auburn 50.2%, ESPN FPI has Auburn 49.6%, numberFire has Auburn 49.5%. All three say coin flip.
evidence.src: Saturday Down South Sep 18; Auburn Wire via Yahoo Sep 17; FanDuel Research Sep 19

evidence.text: The sharper book devigs put Auburn at 46.7%–47.2%: Caesars −120/+105 gives 47.21% at only 3.33% hold, FanDuel −126/+105 gives 46.67%, the SportsLine-quoted −125/+105 gives 46.75%. Kalshi asks 45¢, normalizing to 44.6% — below all of them.
evidence.src: VegasInsider grid and FanDuel Research, Sep 19 2026

evidence.text: The arithmetic. Blending the three coin-flip models with the sharp book devig gives roughly 48%-49% true for Auburn. At a 45¢ ask that is a 3-4¢ edge. The fee is 0.07 × 0.45 × 0.55 = 1.74¢ a contract, so the net is about +1.5 to +2.2¢. Weight SP+ in at 15% and the edge falls to roughly the fee — that is how thin this is.

Why SP+ is discounted rather than averaged in. It is the lone outlier at Florida 63%, it is dated Sep 14, and it is rating Florida on two blowouts of Florida Atlantic and Campbell. Averaging a stale outlier against three current neutral models would be the wrong treatment.

Supporting structure, deliberately NOT counted in the probability estimate: 70% of spread tickets on Florida with the number static all week, VSiN flagging an expected sharp Auburn buyback, Auburn getting both starting edge rushers back, Aaron Philo making his first career road start in a sold-out Jordan-Hare, Florida 0-6 outside The Swamp in 2025 and winless at Auburn in 27 years.
evidence.src: TheSpread Sep 19; VSiN Sep 14; SI/Auburn Daily Sep 17

evidence.text: The math at this size: 3,000 contracts at 45¢ = $1,350, fee $51.98, $1,401.98 tied up. Wins +$1,598.02 if Auburn wins; break-even 46.73¢. Expected profit at a true 48.5%: roughly +$53.
